newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Foreign direct investment booming in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Foreign direct investment booming in Kazakhstan.

text.p: Foreign direct investment is booming in former Soviet Kazakhstan, more than doubling to $3.24 billion as of mid-1996 compared to early in 1994, a report by the U.N. Economic Commission for Europe (ECE) said on Tuesday.

Based on Kazakh central bank data, the ECE, which is the specialised United Nations agency for economic cooperation in Europe, said foreign direct investment in the vast mineral-rich country grew from $1.27 billion at the start of 1994.

The oil-rich but landlocked country stretching from the Chinese border to the east to the Urals to the west, now had more than 800 foreign investors compared to only 14 in 1992, and that number has been growing by several hundred every year.
More than 27,000 Kazakhs now worked for foreign companies or joint ventures compared to some 6,400 in early 1993, the bulk in capital Almaty, the ECE report said.
As of end-1995, loans by foreign investors to their Kazakh joint ventures accounted for nearly 90 percent of the inflow.

U.S. investors led the way with a share of 66 percent worth some $1.8 billion in foreign direct investment at the start of 1996, while West European companies had a share of only 17 percent worth some $456 million, the report said.
U.S. firms have been attracted to Kazakhstan's oil industry, where reserves are officially estimated at 24 billion tonnes.
South Korean companies were the second largest foreign direct investors with a nine percent share, followed by Britain with six and Turkey and France with about four percent each.
The ECE report said the Kazakh oil and natural gas industry had attracted more than 75 percent of the total foreign direct investment, followed by manufacturing with some 24 percent.
The share of foreign investment in banking and telecommunications remained very small.
